source_text.body:
Re-engage unanswered applicants and schedule screening calls overnight
A recruiting agent scanned an ATS for past applicants who never got a response and scheduled 9 screening calls using mutual calendar availability.
·
Jun 12, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The post says an overnight recruiting agent worked from the ATS and calendars while the team was offline. It scanned past applicants for similar roles who never got a response, re-engaged those still in market, then proposed and confirmed screening calls using mutual calendar availability so recruiters arrived to booked invites; the recruiter’s role was to review and decide on candidates the agent had already surfaced.
How it went
In the example, it scheduled 9 screening calls overnight and contributed to a Monday pipeline with 40 screened candidates across 4 roles, including 12 flagged as strong matches. The post gives no breakdown of failures for the re-engagement step itself.
Worth knowing
The source frames this as a workflow teams reported after running agentic recruiting processes for 90 days or more, not an instant first-night result.
Try it yourself
with
Zapier Agents
Copy prompt
Connect to my applicant tracking system, [ATS name], and find candidates who applied for [role or any role] in the last [number] months and never received a response. For each one, draft a short, friendly re-engagement email and propose screening call times from my calendar, [calendar name], and the candidate's reply. Show me the list of candidates and the draft emails first, and do not send any message or create calendar invites until I approve.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GCCrecruiters/comments/1tjcs25/heres_what_actually_happens_when_your_recruiting
